text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Expand medicare, panel to urge: Top advisers tell Ottawa to put brakes to program of trimming transfers to provinces.
- Natives scorn killers' sentences: White men get 6 and a half years each.
- Tumors linked to '50s polio vaccine: Shots infected with monkey virus.
- Ontario to impose civil case mediation: Family disputes exempt in overhaul.
- Hong Kong couple anxious about moving to Canada: Unlike the wealthy immigrants scorned by some, the Yuens are just an ordinary family with ordinary worries.
- Barrick steps up Busang efforts: Hires spokesman, offers junket, while Placer's campaign hits snag.
- CanWest plans U.S. beachhead: Asper says no TV asset is 'too outrageous' to pursue in attractive market south of the border.
- Hibernia embroiled in legal spat: Ottawa, Murphy Oil suing partners over cost-sharing rules.
- This way to the cash, Conrad and Pierre: The names of well-known Canadians can be found on a Web site that locates money left in dormant bank accounts.
- Placer gets Bre-X setback: Indonesian mines minister suggests Placer may not be welcome to participate in huge Busang gold find, no matter how sweet a deal it offers.
- Alberta to challenge Ottawa if MMT ban made law.
